markers.title: Status pill/dropdown too small to tap
markers.body: Each room's status badge (e.g. "Needs deep clean" with a chevron) is the primary interactive control for changing cleaning status, but its text/icon bounding box is only ~16-30dp tall. Increase the pill's vertical padding to hit the ≥44dp touch-target minimum, since this is repeated on every row of the list.

markers.title: Filter chips undersized for tapping
markers.body: The "22 dirty rooms", "11 deep cleans needed" and "0 awaiting inspection" filter chips render at roughly 15-34dp tall, well under the 44dp minimum for a tappable filter control. Add more vertical padding to each chip.

markers.title: Fourth filter chip sits off-screen
markers.body: "0 has notes" is positioned at x=493 in a 390pt-wide viewport, so it's entirely off-canvas. There's no partial-chip peek or scroll indicator hinting the filter row scrolls horizontally, so this filter is effectively undiscoverable.

markers.title: Clean vs deep-clean rely on colour shade alone
markers.body: "Needs deep clean" and "Needs clean" pills use the same red/pink palette differentiated only by a subtle shade/saturation change, with identical layout and no icon difference. This is hard to scan quickly and fails for colour-vision-deficient users; add a distinct icon or label weight to separate the two severities.

markers.title: Header action icons under touch-target size
markers.body: The three header icon buttons next to the date (filter/calendar/settings) each measure roughly 20-22dp square — below the 44×44dp minimum — and sit close together, increasing mis-tap risk on a busy housekeeping screen.

working_well: Room rows keep a consistent 82px vertical rhythm from top to bottom, making the list easy to scan.
Status pills are right-aligned to a shared edge regardless of label length, giving the list a clean visual column.
Room name and room-type label are clearly stacked with a strong hierarchy (bold name, muted caption type).
worth_considering: Consider a sticky/collapsible summary bar so the dirty/deep-clean counts stay visible while scrolling the long room list.
Grouping rows by room type (Family Room, Bridge Room, Deluxe Suite) with section headers could reduce scanning effort versus a single flat list.
A small trailing arrow/fade on the filter-chip row would hint that more chips are scrollable off-screen.
